before.exam_tip_html: The key examiner tip for this topic is the interrelation requirement. For 6-, 8-, or 10-mark questions, the mark scheme rewards candidates who show how life factors, lifestyle choices, and life events work together to affect PIES — not who lists them separately. Use a chaining scaffold: “Because of [life factor], the individual was more likely to make [lifestyle choice], which then [PIES impact] — and when [life event] occurred, this was further complicated by …” Also: the spec distinguishes binge drinking from alcohol abuse from alcohol dependence — use the correct term for the stimulus you are given. A common error is calling any heavy drinking “dependence” when the scenario only describes a single session or a recent bereavement.
